input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across all invocations, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated coroutine corrupt each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two tasks await the same decorated async function concurrently, e.g. via asyncio.gather. Mechanism: stats.clear() on the shared dict resets state that the other in-flight call is still updating, and the dict is mutated across interleaved awaits. Impact: statistics seen by one call's callbacks or by the caller reflect the other call's attempts and timings.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: one shared statistics dict is cleared and reused across calls, so concurrent awaits overwrite each other's statistics through stats.clear(). It only covers the async case, but the label explicitly includes concurrent awaits of the async wrapper.
